questions.q: What are public facilities, and why should the government provide them?
answer: Public facilities are the essential services needed by the whole community, such as water, electricity, sanitation, public transport, schools and healthcare.

answer.text: They are basic to leading a decent life and are needed in large amounts by many people together. Access to safe drinking water, for instance, has been recognised by the courts as part of the Right to Life under Article 21.

Because private companies work for profit, they may not provide these services to those who cannot pay, leaving out the poor. The government, funded by taxes, is expected to provide public facilities to everyone equally, so that even the poorest have access.

answer: This makes the government's role in supplying public facilities essential to fairness and dignity.

questions.q: Why is access to public facilities unequal, and what concerns arise from privatisation?

answer.text: Although public facilities are meant for everyone, access is often unequal in practice. Well-off neighbourhoods usually receive regular piped water, reliable electricity and good sanitation, while poor areas may depend on water tankers, distant taps or have no proper drainage at all.

Some services are being handed over to private companies, which aim to make a profit and therefore charge higher prices. This raises the worry that essential facilities like water may become unaffordable for the poor, defeating the purpose of providing them to all.
The challenge is to ensure that everyone, rich or poor, gets fair and affordable access to these basic services.
